plain: The wall mixes four questions. The record arrow (later means more records) already follows from permanence for every history, and since 2026-07-04 the axiom 'Records form' removes the empty-history escape the entry cites; the June 'reversal' comes from a unitary toy whose records its own second pass erases. What is left is whether matter's arrow follows record births (T03's fork) plus a first state and a random-order formation measure (T01).
best_route: Ask whether record births act on the matter wave (T03 horn 1) instead of why the past was low; the symmetric-blank reading (R1) prices the boundary at zero bits but needs T01's random-order measure.
test: Four scripts: June toy's second pass erases its records; 6-ring: empty is the only symmetric configuration but the symmetry-loss Lyapunov failed (79,596 of 605,052 births raise symmetry); 2D growth: symmetric start homogeneous, 4 seeds not (plateau 1.63/1.08 vs 8.91); 8 qubits: passive births keep start-dependent alignment (dS +1.47 Neel, -1.47 reversed), active locks drive energy toward equilibrium from every start.
cheaper_question: Which arrow is asked for? Record inclusion is settled by permanence. For matter: do record births act on the wave (T03 horn 1: energy runs toward equilibrium from any start, at T03's bond-energy price) or not (the wave needs its own far-from-equilibrium start)? Remaining named residuals: a first state (or past-infinite growth) and a random-order formation measure (T01).
